description: Two-panel composite of engineering stress–strain curves recorded in tension at room temperature. Both panels share identical axes: "Engineering stress [MPa]" on the ordinate from 0 to 800 with gridlines every 100 MPa, and "Engineering strain [%]" on the abscissa drawn with tick marks but no printed numeric strain values. (a) holds five horizontally offset curves: 1 Fe–15Al, 2 Fe–15Al–2Ti–1C, 3 Fe–15Al–2V–1C, 4 Fe–15Al–2Nb–1C, 5 Fe–15Al–2Ta–1C; each rises almost linearly and then falls nearly vertically, i.e. fracture with negligible uniform elongation. Curve 5 attains the highest peak (level with the 700 MPa gridline), curve 4 the next highest (around the 500 MPa level), while curves 1–3 fail between the 300 and 400 MPa gridlines. (b) holds seven offset curves: 6 Fe–26Al, 7 Fe–26Al–2Ti–1C, 8 Fe–26Al–4Ti–1C, 9 Fe–26Al–2V–1C, 10 Fe–26Al–2Nb–1C, 11 Fe–26Al–4Nb–1C, 12 Fe–26Al–2Ta–1C; curves 6 and 11 peak between the 500 and 600 MPa gridlines, whereas curves 8 and 9 fail below the 300 MPa gridline. Filled circles denoting σ0.2 appear in both panels and a bracket labelled "2.5% ε" at bottom right gives a strain scale. The figure shows that all these Fe–Al–M–C alloys are extremely brittle, failing with only a few percent total elongation.

subfigures.description: Engineering stress–strain curves of five Fe–15Al-based alloys, curves 1–5 (1 Fe–15Al, 2 Fe–15Al–2Ti–1C, 3 Fe–15Al–2V–1C, 4 Fe–15Al–2Nb–1C, 5 Fe–15Al–2Ta–1C), each drawn with a horizontal offset for clarity. All show linear elastic loading then an abrupt vertical load drop; curve 5 reaches the 700 MPa gridline, curve 4 about 500 MPa, curves 1–3 between 300 and 400 MPa. Filled circles mark σ0.2; a bracket labelled 2.5% ε and an unlabelled horizontal line at ~400 MPa with a vertical drop line at the right are also drawn.

Engineering stress–strain curves of seven Fe–26Al-based alloys, curves 6–12 (6 Fe–26Al, 7 Fe–26Al–2Ti–1C, 8 Fe–26Al–4Ti–1C, 9 Fe–26Al–2V–1C, 10 Fe–26Al–2Nb–1C, 11 Fe–26Al–4Nb–1C, 12 Fe–26Al–2Ta–1C), horizontally offset. Curves 6 and 11 peak between the 500 and 600 MPa gridlines, curves 7 and 12 somewhat lower, and curves 8 and 9 fracture below the 300 MPa gridline. Filled circles mark σ0.2 and a bracket labelled 2.5% ε sets the strain scale.

observations.observation: Both panels plot engineering stress in MPa (ordinate, 0–800, gridlines every 100 MPa) against engineering strain in % (abscissa); the strain axes carry tick marks but no printed numeric values.
Panel (a) contains five offset curves labelled 1 Fe–15Al, 2 Fe–15Al–2Ti–1C, 3 Fe–15Al–2V–1C, 4 Fe–15Al–2Nb–1C and 5 Fe–15Al–2Ta–1C.
Panel (b) contains seven offset curves labelled 6 Fe–26Al, 7 Fe–26Al–2Ti–1C, 8 Fe–26Al–4Ti–1C, 9 Fe–26Al–2V–1C, 10 Fe–26Al–2Nb–1C, 11 Fe–26Al–4Nb–1C and 12 Fe–26Al–2Ta–1C.
Every curve in both panels consists of an approximately linear elastic rise terminated by an abrupt, near-vertical load drop, i.e. fracture with essentially no uniform plastic elongation.
In panel (a) curve 5 (Fe–15Al–2Ta–1C) reaches the highest peak, level with the 700 MPa gridline, and curve 4 (Fe–15Al–2Nb–1C) the next highest, around the 500 MPa level.
In panel (b) curves 6 (Fe–26Al) and 11 (Fe–26Al–4Nb–1C) peak between the 500 and 600 MPa gridlines, while curves 8 (Fe–26Al–4Ti–1C) and 9 (Fe–26Al–2V–1C) fracture below the 300 MPa gridline.
Filled black circles on the curves, keyed by the legend entry '• σ0.2', mark the 0.2% proof stress in both panels.
A horizontal bracket labelled '2.5% ε' at the bottom right of each panel provides the strain scale reference.

Panel (a) additionally shows an unlabelled horizontal line near the 400 MPa level running to the right-hand side, where a vertical line drops to the strain axis; its meaning is not stated in the caption.
The caption states that the curves are engineering stress–strain curves of Fe–15Al-based (a) and Fe–26Al-based (b) alloys tested at room temperature in tension.
The citing text states that the ductility of most Fe–Al–M–C alloys is very poor and that some alloys crack even during elastic deformation.

The citing text states that, apart from the binary Fe–15Al alloy, the highest total elongations were obtained for Fe–15Al–2Ti–1C and Fe–26Al–2Nb–1C, although the individual elongation values are not printed on the figure.
No numeric value of elongation, proof stress or peak stress is printed anywhere on the figure; values can only be inferred from curve positions relative to the 100 MPa gridlines.

unreadable_items: No numeric values are printed on the 'Engineering strain [%]' axes of either panel; only unlabelled tick marks are present
Curves 1–5 in (a) and 6–12 in (b) are plotted with arbitrary horizontal offsets, so absolute strain positions cannot be read from the axis
The horizontal line at ~400 MPa and the associated vertical line at the right-hand side of panel (a) are unexplained by the caption
σ0.2 dots for curves 4, 5 (a) and 12 (b) are not clearly distinguishable at the supplied resolution
